name: pdk-jsonsubschema-schema
instr:
Our schema registry checks each new version of an event schema against the one before it with jsonsubschema, the library in /app: `isSubschema(old, new)` must be True for a backward compatible change, and we also look at `isSubschema(new, old)`. A copy of the registry and our check are in /data/registry (`python /data/registry/check_registry.py`).

The old versions are draft-04, most without `$schema`. Teams now publish draft-06 and draft-07 versions, and the check fails on nearly all of them, although they are valid schemas. It also fails on a few valid old draft-04 versions.

Please make isSubschema and isEquivalent read each schema under the draft its `$schema` declares (none still means draft-04), so the answers follow what each schema means under its own draft, also across drafts. A newer draft schema and the same schema written in draft-04 should come out equivalent. Every `$ref` has to resolve the way the schema's own draft says, within that version alone, whatever was checked before or sits on the other side. A reference to something the version doesn't contain should raise jsonref's JsonRefError, and nothing may be fetched over the network. A schema that isn't valid under its own draft, such as a draft-07 schema with `"exclusiveMinimum": true`, should raise jsonschema's SchemaError, as invalid draft-04 schemas do today. isSubschema must leave the schema objects it gets unchanged. Draft-04 checks that work today must keep their answers, and the existing tests in /app/
